From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP + cost checks request

Michael — thanks, appreciated. Internal note: looping Jordan for ops assumptions and Laura for procurement timing.

Quick summary below and attached a draft MAP (redwood_map_draft_v1.pdf) and an econ checklist (econ-checklist.xlsx) with prescriptive tests. High level:
- Demo model: small-llama-13B-int8 variant (latency / cost tradeoff).
- Tokens per conv: demo assumed median 280 tokens per request (prompt+response) and 95th pct 1,050 tokens (includes long follow-ups). See attached traffic sample.
- Token/$: we modeled tokens-per-dollar using two axes: model variant (int8 vs fp16) and batching profile. Baseline used int8 throughput on A100-style instance with continuous batching. Baseline unit: ~0.00018 USD per token (median mix) — this is a demo estimate only; please run the checklist tests to validate for your traffic.
- Caching notes: prefix caching for stable system prompts reduces token volume by ~18–30% in our sample workflows. KV-cache reuse on multi-turn reduces per-turn generation by ~40% for follow-ups that reuse context.
- Batching: we recommend validating tail-latency at microbatch sizes 1, 4, 8 and steady-state batching to match your SLA. Batching increases throughput but can change p95 latency; checklist identifies acceptable p95 thresholds.

Next steps I propose:
1) We'll run a short smoke sim (ours) using your attached traffic and send a tokenized breakdown (tokens by type: system/prompt/response) by EOD Wed (2026-07-03).
2) You run the econ-checklist tests during pilot (we included exact request traces to run).
3) Procurement sync with Laura to lock timeline and PO terms.

Resources attached and a HubSpot link in metadata. If useful, we can do a 30m call tomorrow to walk the checklist.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Rohan — quick ops notes (from demo telemetry + expected sims).

On Thu Jul 2 10:05:00 -0700 2026, Rohan Mehta wrote:
> - Tokens per conv: demo assumed median 280 tokens per request (prompt+response) and 95th pct 1,050 tokens (includes long follow-ups).
> - Token/$: baseline used int8 throughput on A100-style instance with continuous batching. Baseline unit: ~0.00018 USD per token (median mix).

My clarifications / recommended checks to add to econ-checklist.xlsx:
- Breakdown tokens into: system prompt (static), user prompt (variable), model response (generated). For many e-health workflows system prompt is large and cacheable — verify percentage of requests where system prompt is identical.
- Validate prefix cache hit rates on your traffic: add a column in the checklist to mark identical prompt hashes. Goal: >25% prefix hit => material savings.
- Run three batching profiles: none (microbatch=1), conservative (microbatch=4, max_delay=10ms), aggressive (microbatch=8, max_delay=30ms). Record p50/p95/p99 latency and cost per 1k requests.
- Measure KV-cache reuse by session id over 3,000 sessions; record average reuse factor.
- Multi-model fallback cost: include a guardrail test that simulates fallback to smaller model on overload and measure accuracy delta.

Also: our demo cost estimate excluded network egress for embeddings-heavy flows; flag if your workflows will embed >10% of conversational payloads — that shifts unit economics.

I can run the smoke sim Rohan mentioned and attach the raw tokenization CSV once complete. Vivek, FYI for quantization/throughput knobs.

—Jordan
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
